sections.body: A CURRENT/CHECKING account is for everyday spending (with a debit card). A SAVINGS account earns interest for money you don't need now.
Check fees, minimum balances and interest rates. Keep your PIN and online banking details private.
The 50/30/20 guideline: about 50% needs (rent, food, transport), 30% wants, 20% savings or paying off debt. Adjust it to your situation.
Build an EMERGENCY FUND: a few months of essential costs, for surprises like losing a job or a repair.

quiz.q: Using the 50/30/20 guideline, how much of a 2,000 monthly income goes to savings?
What is an emergency fund for?
options: Unexpected costs like repairs or job loss
hints: A spare tyre in a car is there for surprise punctures. An emergency fund is like that for money.
quiz.explain: An emergency fund covers unexpected costs so you don't have to borrow.

quiz.q: You want to put aside money you won't need for a year, and earn some interest on it. Which fits best?
options: Cash kept in a drawer at home
hints: One kind of account is designed for everyday spending with a debit card; another is designed for money you're putting aside.
Which option is meant to pay interest on money you leave alone?
Worked example: your weekly bus fares and groceries are paid by debit card, so that money belongs in the account you spend from every day. Money you won't touch for a year has a different job.
quiz.explain: A savings account is designed for money you don't need now and pays interest. A current/checking account is for everyday spending, and cash at home earns nothing and can be lost or stolen. Compare fees and interest rates before choosing.
